george-whitesides.text: Campaign site lists among his priorities in Congress: "protecting a woman's right to choose."
Campaign site lists among his priorities: "protecting Social Security and Medicare for seniors."
House issues page: Health priorities are protecting access to affordable healthcare, supporting local hospitals, and defending reproductive rights.
House issues page: supports "cost-effective, clean energy policies that achieve American energy independence," leveraging private-sector innovation to reduce costs and create jobs.
House issues page: wants "every child has access to high-quality, affordable education regardless of their zip code," investing in public education, community colleges and workforce development.
House issues page: priorities include policies that lower costs and expand job growth for working families, and addressing catastrophic wildfire prevention and the home fire insurance crisis.
Voted Nay on passage of H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (House vote, May 22, 2025).

source.title: House Roll Call 145 (2025), H.R. 1 On Passage

george-whitesides.text: Voted No on the motion to concur in the Senate amendment to H.R. 1, the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (July 3, 2025).

source.title: House Roll Call 190 (2025), H.R. 1 Motion to Concur

george-whitesides.text: Voted Nay on passage of H.R. 5103, the Make the District of Columbia Safe and Beautiful Act (March 25, 2026).

source.title: House Roll Call 101 (2026), H.R. 5103 On Passage

george-whitesides.text: Voted Nay on H.R. 4, the Rescissions Act of 2025 (June 12, 2025).

jason-gibbs.text: Campaign site: "Jason will fight to lower the cost of living by opposing new taxes, supporting energy affordability, and holding government accountable for wasteful spending."
Campaign site: will support law enforcement and oppose "soft-on-crime" policies; "He'll push to end catch-and-release justice and restore consequences for criminal behavior."
Campaign site: "supports securing the border, cracking down on fentanyl trafficking, and ending policies that reward illegal entry"; believes in legal immigration.
Campaign site: local communities "know best how to manage housing, schools, and public safety"; he'll stand up against one-size-fits-all mandates from Sacramento and Washington.
Campaign site: "every parent deserves a say in what their kids are being taught"; he'll work to expand career pathways and technical training, not only four-year-college tracks.
Campaign site: opposes new taxes and one-size-fits-all mandates while supporting energy affordability.

Stated position: "immigration policy should begin with real border security, including secured barriers and protected ports of entry," plus "shorter backlogs, improved legal pathways, and support for skilled and essential workers."
Campaign materials state: "our national debt is a multi-generational economic and security threat."

source.title: Candidate for the 27th Congressional District, Jason Gibbs - LA County Lincoln Clubs

jason-gibbs.text: Listed as the recommended U.S. House District 27 candidate by the California ProLife Council for the 2026 primary.
